chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a garment, then returned it to its owner, but the owner refused to accept it back except for a small amount (a discount). He (AS) said: 'It is not suitable for him except to take it for that small amount. If he was ignorant and took it, then sold it for more than its price, he must return to the first owner the excess.'

key_terms.وَضِيعَةٍ: A small amount or discount; a reduced price

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a seller refuses to take back a returned item at the original price?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanism of *Khiyar al-Shart* (option of condition) or mutual agreement in resale, establishing that the seller's refusal to accept the full original price constitutes a valid new contract at the reduced rate. It further introduces the principle of unjust enrichment (*Ghurm bi Ghurm*), requiring the buyer to disgorge any profit made from reselling the item if he was unaware of the reduced price obligation, ensuring fairness in commercial transactions.
